San Francisco, California · stay

Hotels in San Francisco for cyclists

Where to sleep in San Francisco when you’re here to ride. Book early for event weekends.

Hotels in San Francisco for cyclists, listed

1 with a bike policy in writing · 5 to ask.

  1. HI San Francisco Fisherman’s Wharf Hostel

    Fort Mason, on the Marina side of the city (Zone 6).

    • Building 240, Fort Mason, San Francisco, CA 94123
    • $
    • Bike: Free indoor bicycle storage in the hostel’s bicycle room; space is limited, first come, first served (its words). E-bikes only with UL or EN 15194 certification, battery attached, no charging indoors.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about HI San Francisco Fisherman’s Wharf Hostel

    The hostel’s own page puts the Golden Gate Bridge 3 miles away. The only place we found with the bike policy in writing: a free indoor bicycle room, first come, first served. Dorms of 4 to 20 beds and private rooms; check-in 3 p.m., out 11 a.m.; no elevator (a historic building; ADA rooms on the main floor); a little free parking, passes first come. HI’s own page shows no rate (Oct 2026).

  2. Lodge at the Presidio

    In the Presidio, at the city end of the bridge (Zone 1).

    • 105 Montgomery Street, San Francisco, CA 94129
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    BookDirectionsWebsite
    More about Lodge at the Presidio

    The Presidio Trust calls it “the closest hotel to the Golden Gate Bridge in the entire city.” Sports Basement, the rental shop, is in the Presidio too, and the bridge’s south end is the start of two weekly rides: Fat Cake Tuesday Headlands and Arsicault (Tuesdays, 6:30 am); Hummingbird All Watts Welcome (intervals) (Tuesdays, 7:05 am). The Trust’s page tags it “Bike Parking” without saying where; the hotel’s own rooms page says nothing about bikes. Parking is a nightly fee; no rate or fee shown (Oct 2026).

  3. Cavallo Point

    Fort Baker, at the Marin end of the Golden Gate Bridge below the Headlands (Zone 1).

    • 601 Murray Circle, Fort Baker, Sausalito, CA 94965
    • $$$$
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Cavallo Point

    The 2026 Cycle to Zero started at Fort Baker. The lodge lends Vintage Electric e-bikes free to guests at the valet stand, first come. Its own pages say nothing about bringing your own bike; Expedia lists “bicycle storage,” so ask. From $866 for one night with taxes and fees on Oct 4, plus a $65 nightly resort fee (Expedia, read Oct 3, 2026).

  4. Beck’s Motor Lodge

    • 2222 Market Street, San Francisco, CA 94114
    • $$
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    BookDirectionsWebsite
    More about Beck’s Motor Lodge

    Market Street in the Castro (Zone 6), on the block where Different Spokes’ Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am) meets, and a mile or so from Valencia Cyclery’s walk-in repair. Family-owned since 1958, with free parking on site. Nothing about bikes on its pages. Check-in 3:30 p.m., out 11 a.m. Rooms from $149 for a Superior Queen (its own site, Oct 2026).

  5. Holiday Inn Express Mill Valley San Francisco Area

    • 160 Shoreline Highway, Mill Valley, CA 94941
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Holiday Inn Express Mill Valley San Francisco Area

    Shoreline Highway in Mill Valley (Zone 2), down the road from Equator Coffees at Proof Lab (244 Shoreline Hwy), the start of Tam Velo Club’s rides: Tam Velo Club Saturday Ride (Saturdays, 8:30 am); Tam Velo Club Sunday Recovery Ride (Sundays, 9:30 am). The page puts the Golden Gate Bridge about 7 miles away. Free adult bikes to borrow; nothing about your own bike. Free parking; breakfast from 6:30 a.m. weekdays, 7 a.m. weekends. No rate shown (Oct 2026).

  6. Mill Valley Inn

    Downtown Mill Valley, the Marin town under Mt. Tamalpais (Zone 2), for a rider who wants to walk to dinner after Tam.

    • 165 Throckmorton Avenue, Mill Valley, CA 94941
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    BookDirectionsWebsite
    More about Mill Valley Inn

    The inn has “Bikes available” for a ride around town, but nothing on its page about your own. Free parking, no resort fee, a breakfast buffet with an espresso bar. No rate shown (Oct 2026).
